A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 27-page versions of the same CARMANIA study. Their main text, figures, tables, Appendices A and B, and checklist support reliable comparison despite relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original genomic benchmark results, training experiments, and ablations of TM loss, attention, model architecture, and sequence length.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds protein-sequence experiments, a Caduceus TM-loss ablation, and a ConvNova comparison.

M1.justification: The core CARMANIA architecture and next-token-plus-TM objective remain unchanged. V2 Appendix A.3 adds a procedural extension that incorporates TM loss into Caduceus's masked-language-model fine-tuning objective, extending beyond the causal training setup.

E1.justification: V2 Appendix A.1 adds training and evaluation on Scorpio-Gene–Taxa protein sequences, extending the represented biological inputs from nucleotides to amino acids. The original genomic datasets and tasks remain; the AMR evaluation is relocated rather than newly added.

E2.justification: V2 adds ConvNova to a separate Genomics Benchmark comparison in Table 16. Table 8 also adds 7.7M-parameter Caduceus variants with and without TM loss to the Scorpio-Gene–Taxa comparison with CARMANIA. Original comparison tables retain their baseline sets.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a controlled fine-tuning experiment using the 7.7M Caduceus variant, a separate evaluation following ConvNova's protocol, and inter-class bigram KL divergence as a diagnostic metric. Original cross-validation protocols remain. Table 1's expanded settings description does not establish that its experiments changed.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends analysis of TM-loss transferability through protein-domain and Caduceus masked-model ablations (Tables 7–8). Section 4.4 additionally examines whether task-specific gains track inter-class bigram separability. Existing HyenaDNA, beta, transition-order, architecture, and sequence-length analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A.9 explicitly specifies five random seeds for the new ConvNova comparison. Existing cross-validation and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish increased repetition of retained experiments or introduce significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds protein results, Caduceus ablation results, and a separate ConvNova comparison. Table 8 reports test gene accuracy of 26.2% without TM versus 38.6% with TM; Table 16 reports mouse-enhancer accuracy of 0.795 for CARMANIA versus 0.784 for ConvNova. Section 4.4 adds KL values of 9.28, 0.99, and 0.64. Original benchmark scores are retained; the added evaluations do not establish performance gains between versions under identical settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and Appendix B's transition-matrix derivation are retained. Expressing fixed-window attention complexity as O(kn) rather than O(n) makes window dependence explicit without introducing a new theoretical result or changing the derivation.

C1.justification: V2's introduction adds the qualified novelty claim that CARMANIA is the longest-context transformer-based genomic language model, supporting contexts up to 160 kbp. The abstract's principal performance claims, contribution list, and conclusion remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: V1 explains H4ac gains through clustered, sequence-specific acetylation patterns. V2 instead argues that TM helps when local features are ambiguous, links gains inversely to bigram separability, and emphasizes diffuse, combinatorial H4 patterns. New appendices also interpret TM loss as applicable to proteins and masked state-space models. Existing beta and memory limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 Table 1 specifies evaluation datasets, 10,000 hg38 fragments, and an absolute reference cost of approximately 16.7 × 10^12 FLOPs per sequence. New appendices disclose the protein 20 × 20 transition matrix and Caduceus model size. Dataset documentation corrects Scorpio's task count from six to ten, matching outputs already reported in v1 Table 4, and removes the AMR class-count range.

R1.justification: V2 adds Bo et al. (2025) for ConvNova and Dion et al. (2005) for H4 acetylation, while removing Jha and Strahl (2014) and Struhl (1998). These support the added comparison and revised biological interpretation; the related-work discussion otherwise remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 expands the introduction's SWA explanation, rewrites the task-specific TM interpretation, moves AMR discussion from Appendix A.1 into Section 4.4, and adds appendix subsections. The overall narrative structure remains intact, and the preprint footer changes to NeurIPS 2025.

P2.justification: V2 adds three tables for proteins, Caduceus, and ConvNova, expands Table 1's caption, and relocates the existing AMR table into the main text. Several figures and tables move with pagination, but all eight figures retain their graphical content and the overall visual format remains stable.

improvement.justification: The protein and Caduceus ablations broaden evidence about TM-loss applicability, while the ConvNova comparison and expanded Table 1 documentation improve evaluation coverage and clarity. These benefits are limited by missing uncertainty in new Tables 7–8 and imprecise interpretation: Table 8 labels percentage-point differences as relative improvements, and the three-task KL association does not establish the asserted long-range mechanism.
